title: Completion of remote and centre-based cardiac rehabilitation: a retrospective comparison of programme records, 2023 to 2025
subtitle: Retrospective comparison of programme records with a single completion definition
statement: Since January 2023 about 38 percent of patients referred for cardiac rehabilitation choose a remote programme instead of the centre-based one. The board is considering making remote rehabilitation the default, but nobody knows whether completion differs between the programmes once the same definition is applied to both, or whether any difference holds for women, older people and people in deprived or remote areas.
whoAffected: Adults referred after a heart attack, a stent or bypass surgery, particularly women, people aged 75 or over, people in deprived areas and people living far from the hospital; rehabilitation staff; the board.
whatHurts: Patients who do not complete rehabilitation lose its benefits; a default chosen without evidence could exclude people who cannot use remote tools or cannot travel.
currentPractice: Patients choose between the centre-based and remote programmes; completion is counted differently in each and is not reported by patient group.
whyNow: The board's April 2027 service review will decide the default programme.
patientCenteredGoal: Every referred patient can complete a rehabilitation programme that fits their life, whichever setting they choose.
summary: Problem framed as a fair retrospective comparison of completion by setting, with equity subgroups.
